ai.title: Add skill support to CLI and agent runtime
ai.summary: Introduces a skill system allowing agents to load on-demand instructions via the new `skill` tool. CLI startup initializes a skill registry from `.agents/skills`, exposing each skill as a dynamic slash command (`/skill:<name>`) and a tool call. The `base2` agent now includes the `skill` tool, enabling it to fetch and apply skill context during execution. Covers core constants, CLI UI components, and SDK loading logic.

eli5.text: The assistant built into the command-line tool can now learn new tricks on the fly. You (or anyone using the tool) can drop instruction files into a special folder, and each one becomes a new command you can run by typing its name. The built-in assistant agent has also been taught to use this system, so it can pull in those instructions during a task, such as asking it to review your uncommitted code changes or clean up messy code. This is live as of the January 26 update.

ai.title: Skip Gravity ads in compact non-free CLI layouts
ai.summary: use-gravity-ad.ts suppresses ad fetching, impression recording, and rendering when terminalHeight <= 17, gated by agentMode !== 'FREE'. Uses shouldHideAdsRef to guard async fetchAd and recordImpressionOnce calls. FREE mode retains mandatory ads on compact screens. Scope limited to CLI Gravity ad hook via use-terminal-layout and useChatStore selectors.

eli5.text: When you run the command-line assistant in a terminal window that is 17 lines tall or shorter, promotional messages no longer appear at the bottom of your screen, unless you are using the free version (where they still show). Behind the scenes, the program now checks the height of your terminal window and quietly skips downloading, tracking, and displaying any ads when there isn't enough space, while keeping them on for free users. This only affects the text-based helper you use in a terminal; the full graphical app is unchanged.

ai.title: CLI loads agents from ~/.agents global directory
ai.summary: initializeAgentRegistry now scans ~/.agents in addition to project and parent directories via getDefaultAgentDirs(). Precedence order is cwd, parent, then home, allowing project agents to override global ones. buildAgentFilePathMap accepts an array of directories instead of a single path. This change affects cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts.

eli5.text: You can now place agent definitions in a single folder in your home directory, and they will be available to every project you work on, not just the current one. The system checks three locations for agents in order: the folder of your current project, the folder of its parent directory, and finally your personal home directory. Whatever an agent in your project folder shares a name with an agent in your home directory, the project one wins, so you can still customize agents for specific projects. This is live today.

ai.title: Bump CLI version to 1.0.600
ai.summary: The CLI release package version increments from 1.0.599 to 1.0.600 in `cli/release/package.json`. This is a release-bump commit bundling prior same-day work: skill support for CLI and agent runtime, Gravity ad suppression in compact non-free layouts, and agent loading from `~/.agents`.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json bumps version field from 1.0.599 to 1.0.600; the +1/-1 diff is a single line change with no functional code

eli5.text: This release introduces a new 'skills' system that lets AI agents load custom instructions on the fly, along with smarter ad display handling and broader agent loading support. You can now drop specially formatted instruction files into a ~/.agents/skills folder, and they'll automatically become available as new commands (like /skill:your-skill-name) that agents can call during conversations, making it easy to extend their capabilities without changing core settings. The CLI now checks a global ~/.agents directory for agent definitions in addition to project-specific ones, so your favorite custom agents will be available everywhere, not just in specific project folders. When working in tight terminal windows, ads are automatically hidden to give you more space for actual work, unless you're in free mode where ads remain shown. Upgrading gives you a more flexible and extensible agent experience, better use of small terminal screens, and unified access to your agents across different projects.

ai.title: Preserve partial responses on request cancel
ai.summary: SDK `run.ts` preserves partial streamed content and appends interruption messages to `sessionState` when `signal.aborted` is true. CLI `send-message.ts` skips `handleRunCompletion` if `wasAbortedByUser` is set, preventing UI interference. Covers SDK core and CLI hooks.

eli5.text: When you cancel an in-progress answer by stopping it mid-stream, the assistant now saves whatever it managed to type before you interrupted and adds a short note explaining that you cancelled. The next time you ask something, the assistant will know the previous reply was cut short and can pick up from there instead of losing that partial work.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.601 preserves partial responses on cancel
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.601 in cli/release/package.json. This release includes the notable improvement where the SDK run.ts preserves partial streamed content and appends interruption messages to sessionState when signal.aborted is true, and the CLI send-message.ts skips handleRunCompletion if wasAbortedByUser is set, preventing UI interference during request cancellation. The change spans SDK core and CLI hooks.
ai.evidence: Commit d826a7ed bumps the version field in cli/release/package.json from 1.0.600 to 1.0.601 (a single-line change, +1/−1). This is the release-bump commit for the 1.0.601 release, which includes the notable user-visible change of preserving partial responses and interruption messages when a request is cancelled via SDK run.ts and CLI send-message.ts.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.601 now keeps the AI's partially typed responses when you stop or cancel a request, instead of throwing away everything you were just reading. If the AI is in the middle of answering and you interrupt (for example, by hitting Esc or sending a new message), your conversation history will still contain that partial reply along with a clear note showing it was cut short, so you never lose context mid-flow. This applies to both the command-line interface and the developer SDK, meaning interruptions stay graceful and predictable across the board. Upgrading makes your daily chats with Freebuff feel smoother and more reliable, since stopping an AI response no longer disrupts your session state or leaves you staring at erased text.

ai.title: Swap ad and referral grant priorities
ai.summary: Reorders `GRANT_PRIORITIES` so `referral` (30) consumes before `ad` (40). Ensures one-time referral bonuses deplete ahead of renewable ad credits. Updates `common/src/constants/grant-priorities.ts` and `packages/billing/src/billing.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: Your account holds two kinds of credits: one-time referral bonuses and renewable ad credits that refresh each month. The assistant now uses one-time referral credits first and draws down ad credits after, so any referral bonus you received gets spent before your recurring ad credit kicks in. This affects the order in which your available credits are used, making referral bonuses deplete ahead of renewable ad credits. The change is live today.

eli5.text: When you paste an image into the CLI chat, it now waits until that image is fully ready before trying to display it. This stops the picture from occasionally showing up blank or glitchy because the program tried to read the file too early, and it also makes sure error messages point to the correct file location when something does go wrong. If you use the CLI to send images today, you just get smoother, more reliable previews.

ai.title: Add build wrapper script for better error logging on Render
ai.summary: Replaced the inline Next.js build command in package.json with a dedicated Bun script, web/scripts/build.ts. This wrapper captures full build output to build.log, filters noisy Contentlayer warnings from console display, and logs timing/memory stats. On failure, the full log is displayed to aid debugging on Render; on success, it triggers prebuild-agents-cache validation.

eli5.text: When the site's pages are built on the hosting platform, the system now records every step in a detailed log file so that if something goes wrong, the full error message is shown instead of being hidden. The build process also filters out repetitive warning messages that used to clutter the screen, and on successful builds it automatically checks that a cache of helper tools is ready. This affects anyone working on or deploying the website, as build failures will now be easier to diagnose.

ai.title: Handle missing database in sitemap and static params fetch
ai.summary: Wrap fetchAgentsForSitemap and fetchAgentsForStaticParams in try/catch blocks in web/src/server/agents-data.ts. Return empty arrays and log warnings when database queries fail, preventing build crashes in CI environments without a database. Scope limited to server-side data fetching utilities. Static params fallback to runtime rendering when database is unavailable.

eli5.text: When the site tries to build its pages automatically, it no longer crashes if the database is missing or slow. Instead, it quietly logs a warning and skips generating those pages, letting them load dynamically when someone visits. This means your builds stay green in environments without a database, and visitors see the pages normally at runtime.

ai.title: Clarify general agent context limitations
ai.summary: Updated `spawnerPrompt` in `agents/general-agent/general-agent.ts` for both GPT-5 and Opus variants. Explicitly states agent cannot see previously read files or discussion history, requiring context via `prompt` or `filePaths`. Internal prompt refinement only.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to solve a problem by spinning up a specialized helper agent, that helper now comes with a clearer warning: it starts each task with no memory of what you've already shown it. It can't see the files you've previously opened or the back-and-forth you've had so far. For the helper to do its best work, you still need to give it the full picture upfront by pasting the relevant text or pointing it at the right files. The wording of this reminder was tweaked slightly for both versions of the helper agent you can summon.

ai.title: Context pruner preserves last user images in summary
ai.summary: Context pruner now extracts and retains `ImagePart`/`FilePart` objects from the most recent user message containing media before generating the `<conversation_summary>`. This prevents loss of visual context during aggressive pruning, ensuring the agent can reference images attached in the latest prompt even after older messages are condensed. The change is isolated to `agents/context-pruner.ts`, modifying the summary construction logic to append preserved media parts to the `UserMessage` content array.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs long conversations, it periodically condenses earlier messages into a short summary to save space. Now, when it does that, it also pulls the most recent image you sent and tucks it back into the summary so the assistant can still see and talk about that picture. So you'll notice the assistant can keep referencing your latest attached image even after the conversation has been heavily condensed. This is live today for anyone using the agent runtime when context pruning kicks in.

ai.title: Fix CLI image sending to use pre-processed data instead of disk
ai.summary: The `processImagesForMessage` function in `cli/src/utils/image-processor.ts` now uses `pendingImages.processedImage` data directly instead of re-reading files from disk. This prevents failures when image paths are relative to a different working directory than the current `cwd`. The logic prioritizes pre-processed base64 data, falling back to disk processing only if `processedImage` is missing but status is 'ready'. Inline image paths detected in message content are processed separately, skipping any already handled by `pendingImages`.

eli5.text: When you attach an image to a message in the CLI, the system no longer re-reads the image file from your computer's hard drive. Instead, it uses the image data that was already prepared when you attached the file, avoiding errors that occurred when image paths were relative to a different working directory than the current one. If you tried to send images before, this fix prevents failures by using pre-processed data directly, and only falls back to reading from disk if the pre-processed data is unexpectedly missing. This affects anyone using the CLI to send images in their conversations.

ai.title: Fix CLI test failures via logger mock and path normalization
ai.summary: CLI integration tests now mock `../../utils/logger` to prevent analytics initialization errors during execution. Path assertions in `local-agents.test.ts` use `realpathSync` to normalize macOS symlink discrepancies between `/var` and `/private/var`. Changes affect `cli/src/__tests__/integration/local-agents.test.ts` and `cli/src/utils/__tests__/image-dimensions.test.ts`. No user-facing behavior changes.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team fixed the automated checks that verify the command-line tool works correctly. These checks were crashing because they tried to turn on usage tracking while running, and they were also failing on Mac computers where file locations get reported differently. The fix tells the checks to skip the usage tracking and to compare file paths in a way that works the same on every computer. You won't notice anything different when using the tool, this just makes sure the developers' testing runs smoothly.

ai.title: Hide copy button on empty user message in CLI
ai.summary: Copy button suppressed when user message text is empty. `UserContentWithCopyButton` now checks `normalizedContent.length > 0` alongside `showCopyButton` in `cli/src/components/blocks/user-content-copy.tsx`. Scope limited to CLI user message blocks. Prevents rendering a non-functional copy affordance for whitespace-only or blank messages.

eli5.text: When you send a blank or whitespace-only message in the CLI, the small copy icon that normally lets you copy your message text no longer appears next to it, because copying nothing isn't useful anyway. Now the system checks whether your message actually contains text before showing that copy button, so you only see the button when it can do something real. You would notice this only if you specifically tried to copy an empty message and looked for a missing icon.
